chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Clubs around Boston Road and George Duvivier
summary: She recalls Harlem and Bronx clubs before moving and mentions Duvivier.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: used to be quite a few clubs around Boston Road. And there was a club up here that was a branch of the Fat Man on Sugar Hill where the musicians used to hang out at after hours. And of course, Fat Man, he was - he had been a bass player with what, Fat Faller? I forget his real name, but he had a place in Harlem on 155th Street. And of course I bought this house from Eddie Mallory who was married to Ethel Waters at one time. And Eddie Mallory was running the Bronx Branch of Fat Man.
You mentioned the name George Duvivier one time.
You and Chester Campbell were talking together and the name George Duvivier came up.

Yeah, well before I moved here I live in Harlem. I lived off of St. Nicholas Avenue on 149th Street and I think George Duvivier still lives in that building, yeah. And of course I lived at the Dorrance-Brooks at one time and that was a house where Lionel Hampton lived and I think he still maintains an apartment there. But now you have two housing projects in Harlem. One named the Lionel Hampton Houses and just recently
